whySaudi.heading: Why Saudi?
paragraphs: Saudi Arabia has recently undergone significant economic reforms, resulting in increased opportunities for foreign investment. The country's rich natural resources, including oil and minerals, make it a prime location for businesses to thrive. In addition, the government's efforts to open up the economy and attract international investment further enhance the attractiveness of Saudi Arabia as a destination for business ventures.

Northman & Sterling is a company that has been serving the region for over 10 years, offering a range of services to support the establishment of businesses in Saudi Arabia. Our 360 degree service delivery model covers all aspects of the process, from the initial formation of the company to post-launch business support. With a wealth of experience and a comprehensive approach, Northman & Sterling is well-equipped to guide investors through the journey of setting up a business in Saudi Arabia. Whether you are a seasoned investor or new to the market, Northman & Sterling can provide the expert assistance and support you need to succeed in the thriving business environment of Saudi Arabia.

ownership.heading: 100% Foreign Ownership
paragraphs: Establishing a branch office in Saudi Arabia can be a strategic move for businesses seeking to expand their operations. The Ministry of Investment of Saudi Arabia (MISA) allows for 100% foreign ownership of branch offices without the need for a local sponsor.
While branch offices are not permitted to engage in trading activities, they can support the parent company's business development in the service industry.

Alternatively, a representative office is a type of branch that is limited to marketing activities on behalf of the parent company, but cannot participate in business development. Both branch offices and representative offices offer opportunities for companies to expand their presence in Saudi Arabia and tap into the country's growing economy.

Branch of a Foreign Company

General partnership
Technical and scientific services office
The sole establishment
entityForms.footerNote: The shareholding structure and required paid-up capital will change based on the company activity and legal form.

entities.name: Limited Liability Company (LLC)

rows.label: Capital Requirements
rows.value: Determined by MISA based on activity and shareholding

rows.label: Losses Exceeding 50% of Capital
rows.value: Shareholders meet within 90 days to decide on business continuation

rows.label: Corporate Taxes on Annual Net Profits
Ability to Bid for Government Contracts
rows.value: Yes, filing an annual tax return is required

recommendedPractices: Seek tax and corporate structuring advice
Engage Northman & Sterling for compliance guidance
Appoint an auditor post company formation

entities.name: Branch of a Foreign Company

rows.label: Limited Liability
rows.value: No, head office bears full liability

rows.label: Losses Exceeding 50% of Capital
rows.value: Shareholders meet within 90 days to decide on business continuation

rows.label: Corporate Taxes on Annual Net Profits
Ability to Bid for Government Contracts
rows.value: Yes, filing an annual tax return is required

keyFeatures: Activities must match the parent company's business
Engage in commercial activities within the license's scope
recommendedPractices: Seek tax and corporate structuring advice
Appoint an auditor once the branch setup is finalized

entities.name: Joint Stock Company (JSC)
entities.note: A JSC is suitable for large multinational companies or those listed on other stock exchanges.

rows.label: Losses Exceeding 50% of Capital
rows.value: Shareholders meet within 45 days to decide on business continuation or increase capital

rows.label: Corporate Taxes on Annual Net Profits
Ability to Bid for Government Contracts
rows.value: Yes, filing an annual tax return is required

termsAndConditions.intro: These terms and conditions ("Agreement") govern the use of Immigration and Visa services offered by Northman & Sterling. By engaging with our services, you agree to comply with these terms and conditions in their entirety.

sections.heading: Scope of Services
sections.body: Northman and Sterling offers professional immigration and visa services to corporates and businesses seeking assistance in various immigration and Visa matters in different regions. Our services include but are not limited to visa processing, residency permits, company registration, legal compliance, and related advisory services.

sections.heading: Client Obligations
sections.body: As a client of Northman, you agree to provide accurate and complete information regarding your immigration or visa requirements. It is your responsibility to ensure the authenticity and validity of all provided documents. Any false or misleading information may result in the termination of our services without liability.

sections.heading: Service Fees and Payment
sections.body: Northman's service fees are disclosed prior to engagement and are based on the specific services requested. All fees quoted are exclusive of any government charges, taxes, or third-party expenses. Payment terms and methods will be discussed and agreed upon with the client. Failure to make timely payments may result in a suspension or termination of services.

sections.heading: Confidentiality
sections.body: We understand the sensitivity of client information and ensure the highest level of confidentiality. We undertake to handle all client data and documents with strict confidentiality, except as required by law or with the client's consent.

sections.heading: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: Northman & Sterling will exercise reasonable care and skill in delivering its services. However, we do not guarantee the outcome of any immigration or Visa application, as the final decision lies with the relevant authorities. We shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, or consequential damages arising from the use or inability to use our services.

sections.heading: Termination of Services
sections.body: Either party may terminate the services by providing written notice to the other party. In the event of termination, any outstanding fees or expenses incurred up to the termination date will be due and payable.
